root_idea.summary: The root centers on guarding, preserving, and keeping watch; a separate reported branch associates it with time or duration.
root_idea.development: The preservation branch extends from guarding and guardianship to guarded objects and self-protection. The theft usage is explained as watching or guarding an object until it can be taken. A duration sense is reported in Classical usage but remains disputed in the supplied evidence.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form حَرَسًا is explicitly identified as a plural of حَارِسٌ, so it is presented under the singular lexical citation form.

senses.definition: Guards or guardians who protect and watch over a place.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form حَرَسًا is the plural of حَارِسٌ and is used here of guarding a place; the lexical branch is especially associated with places rather than valuables and goods.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To guard, protect, preserve, keep, or take care of someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical Form I verb; حِرَاسَةٌ is used for the act of guarding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To steal, especially livestock or something taken from pasture by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or ironic usage; the sources vary over the precise object and circumstances of the theft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A period of time or a long duration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported and disputed interpretation of a poetic occurrence; it is not the Quranic sense of the form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become provided with guards or come to have a guard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical Form IV usage expressing becoming possessed of guards.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To guard oneself against someone or something; to protect oneself against it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Normally construed with مِنْ; it denotes self-protection or precaution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stolen things, especially livestock taken successively and eaten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in the plural idiom الحِرَاسَاتِ describing repeated theft of sheep or goats and consumption of what was stolen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something guarded, kept, preserved, or taken care of.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An affected or protected object noun, without a restriction to a particular object class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing stolen, especially livestock taken by night from a mountain or pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage with differing explanations: it may denote the stolen thing itself or an animal that was insufficiently protected.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone wall or enclosure made to guard sheep or goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete protective structure for livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A guardian or keeper; also guards collectively, including a ruler’s guards.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote an individual guardian or function as a collective designation for guards.
An ironic or figurative usage based on the notion that supposed guardians may themselves steal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Someone against whom one guards oneself; by extension, an entrusted guardian from whom one is not safe because he may betray the trust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in a proverbial construction contrasting a person who requires protection from someone who is himself called a guardian.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the Form I guarding and preserving branch.
Covers guarding oneself against someone or something.
Covers the idiom for repeatedly stolen livestock or things.
Covers the protected or guarded object.
Covers the stolen-thing and stolen-livestock branch.
Covers the livestock-protecting stone wall or enclosure.
Covers guardian, keeper, and collective guards.
Covers the proverbial untrustworthy guardian construction.

cautions: The duration or time sense of حَرَسٌ is reported from a poetic interpretation but is disputed in the supplied discussion and does not apply to the Quranic occurrence.
The theft senses are marked figurative, ironic, or debated in the lexical evidence and are distinct from the ordinary guarding branch.
